title: 6.23.3 Lab: Take turns to the finish
description: Two players, one die: roll, move, pass the turn, and stop on the last square to win.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: This is your board from 6.22.4. One token steps one square for each SPACE.

steps.title: Two players
steps.instructions: Add `let players;`, `let turn = 0;`, `let message = 'Press SPACE to roll';` and `let winner = -1;` at the top. Write `newGame()`: it fills `players` with two objects like `{ name: 'Red', color: 'tomato', at: 0 }`, and sets `turn` to 0, `winner` to -1 and the message back. Call it at the end of `setup()`.
hints: If you brought your 6.22.4 work forward, your names may differ; keep yours.
A colour can be any name the canvas knows: `'tomato'`, `'dodgerblue'`, `'gold'`.

steps.title: Draw the players
steps.instructions: Take out the one tomato token and the `at` variable. Write `drawPlayers()`, which loops over `players` and draws each one's circle on `path[players[p].at]`, moved sideways by `p * 20`. Call it in `draw()` after `drawBoard()`. In `drawTop()`, show `message` and whose turn it is: `players[turn].name + "'s turn"`.

steps.title: Roll and take a turn
steps.instructions: Write `takeTurn(r)` from the reading: move `players[turn]` by `r` with `min(p.at + r, last)`, set the message, stop with a winner on the last square, and otherwise pass the turn with `%`. In `draw()`, SPACE calls `takeTurn(floor(random(1, 7)))` while `winner === -1`.
hints: Without `min`, a big roll near the end sends the token off the board, and `path[33]` does not exist.
Pass the turn in its own `nextTurn()`: day three adds to it.

steps.title: R starts again
steps.instructions: In `draw()`, `if (kb.presses('r') && winner !== -1) newGame();`. Play a whole game to the finish, then press R.

requirements.title: A roll from 1 to 6
requirements.description: The die gives a whole number from 1 to 6. Help: 6.23.1 (Reading: A die, and whose turn it is)

requirements.title: A list of players
requirements.description: The players are a list of objects, each with its own square. Help: 6.23.1 (Reading: A die, and whose turn it is)

requirements.title: The turn passes
requirements.description: The turn moves to the next player and wraps back to 0, with % players.length or another way. Help: 6.23.1 (Reading: A die, and whose turn it is)

requirements.title: Never past the last square
requirements.description: A roll near the end stops on the last square, with min or a check. Help: 6.23.1 (Reading: A die, and whose turn it is)

requirements.title: A winner on the last square
requirements.description: Reaching the last square ends the game with a winner. Help: 6.23.1 (Reading: A die, and whose turn it is)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Lab: Take turns to the finish". The task: turn the one-token board into a race for two: a list of player objects, a die from 1 to 6, a takeTurn that moves the player whose turn it is without going past the last square, a winner on the last square, the turn passed to the next player, and R to start again. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: Players in a list

rubric.title: Turns pass

rubric.title: Stays on the board
rubric.description: A big roll stops on the last square.

rubric.title: A winner
rubric.description: Reaching the last square ends the game.
